html:
The Albanian unrest of 1997 began in January when a set of pyramid investment schemes collapsed, wiping out the savings of a large share of the population, and grew into armed revolt and near state collapse.

The schemes had paid high monthly interest from new deposits and were linked to people close to the government. When they failed, crowds attacked government buildings, first in the south around Vlorë. Army depots were looted and hundreds of thousands of weapons spread across the country. About 2,000 people were killed. President Sali Berisha's government fell, an Italian led force restored order, and early elections brought the Socialists to power. Many of the looted guns later reached the Kosovo War, and the crisis drove more emigration from Albania.
sum: The Albanian unrest of 1997 began in January when a set of pyramid investment schemes collapsed, wiping out the savings of a large share of the population, and grew into armed revolt and near state collapse.
